PullRequest.Title: Fix auto model not being properly restored
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or reconnect to an existing agent-host chat session and restore completed plus active turns
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing agent-host session and chat subscriptions must hydrate before history conversion. The changed model-ID resolution then runs synchronously while each turn is converted; existing subagent-history enrichment follows and may await child hydration. The added lookup does not add an await or boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Hydrate the agent-host session-state and chat-state subscriptions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two root hydration operations per opened session (session state and chat state), subject to existing shared-subscription reuse
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two hydrations were required before the diff; the changed model lookup runs only after they complete
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both hydrations complete before restored history can be built

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch ChatDraftChanged when synthesizing a missing draft
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero or one fire-and-forget dispatch per restored session
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited and therefore off the restoration critical path

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Hydrate existing child session and child chat subscriptions used by restored subagent enrichment
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one session/chat hydration pair per distinct restored child chat, with existing subscription reuse
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same child hydration fan-out existed before the diff; changed model metadata does not alter child discovery or subscription count
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing enrichment awaits child hydration before restored subagent details are complete

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of completed turns T, plus optional distinct restored child chats C. The diff adds one in-memory actual-model lookup for each turn that has usage and one for an active turn; existing IPC remains grouped by root session/chat and distinct child chat.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Completed turns are converted serially in the existing loop. Root subscription hydrations remain sequentially awaited; child subscription behavior is pre-existing. The diff adds no queue, Promise, fan-out, or concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Language-model resolution uses LanguageModelsService._modelCache.get. Warm registered models are O(1) Map hits; cold or unregistered identifiers are bounded Map misses followed by string namespacing, with no provider activation, network, or filesystem read. No new cache or retained key is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the added work is O(T), synchronous, bounded, and boundary-free, based on turnsToHistory and lookupLanguageModel's direct Map.get implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sessions can have many historical turns, but each added operation is a bounded regex/string normalization and at most two in-memory Map lookups; no evidence indicates a material load-time cost even for long histories.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: model metadata enrichment adds only bounded in-memory work per already-converted turn and does not change critical-path IPC cardinality or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Receive live usage updates while an agent-host turn is running, including Auto resolving to a concrete model
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An existing inbound ChatUsage state update invalidates the usage observable. The changed code resolves actualModelId with a bounded in-memory lookup, compares it during deduplication, and forwards a usage part only when tracked usage fields change. No new asynchronous work blocks the turn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive an agent-host ChatUsage action and replace active-turn usage state
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inbound action per reported model call or later usage refinement/routing update; effective count is the host's existing usage-event count
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same ChatUsage actions crossed the agent-host boundary before the diff
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The inbound update is the trigger; the added lookup happens after receipt and adds no round trip

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of usage reports U in one active turn, generally model-call and refinement events rather than token-stream events. The diff adds one bounded actual-model resolution per report and can forward the one-time transition from unknown to known actual model.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable autoruns process state updates synchronously in sequence. The diff adds no parallel lookup, IPC request, limiter, or burst mechanism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each resolution consults the already-populated language-model Map. Missing registrations remain bounded misses with no negative-cache need because no expensive boundary is crossed. No values are retained beyond existing lastUsage state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the reducer, usage observable, model lookup implementation, and sink path that no boundary or collection-wide work was added.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact usage-event counts vary with subagents and refinements, but the per-event delta is small constant CPU/allocation and the existing host events dominate; no realistic high-frequency token/frame loop was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added Map lookup and string normalization are constant-time per existing usage event, while downstream usage updates were already driven by those events.

Scenarios.Scenario: Update the context-usage widget after usage/model metadata changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A response change synchronously recomputes the effective model, reads cached model metadata/configuration, calculates percentages, and updates a small fixed set of DOM properties. actualModelId selects the correct existing metadata path; it does not add a renderer, layout query, or collection traversal.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct forwarded usage updates for the latest response. Work is fixed per update and independent of session-history size; actualModelId itself adds no extra DOM nodes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous single-widget updates on the UI thread; no concurrent rendering or queued burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Model metadata is a direct in-memory Map lookup. Existing model-configuration lookup behavior is unchanged. Cold missing metadata returns immediately and waits for the pre-existing model-registration event rather than initiating I/O.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the downstream work is fixed-size and boundary-free from chatContextUsageWidget.updateFromResponse/render and ChatResponseModel usage handling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact DOM-update frequency follows existing usage reports. The handler's new actual-model comparison can distinguish a model-resolution refinement, but this is bounded to model metadata changes and does not establish repeated frame-level work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff supplies richer model metadata to an existing fixed-cost widget update path without increasing DOM size, forcing layout reads, or introducing unbounded render frequency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and all diff pages. Traced restoration, active-turn reconnection, live usage propagation, language-model lookup, deduplication, and context-widget rendering. The PR adds bounded in-memory model-ID resolution and metadata fields but no material CPU, memory, UI, cache-lifecycle, concurrency, or expensive-boundary regression; no findings or regression-fix records were warranted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
